title: Steve Lewis, his first drum teacher, and the Piron band
summary: Steve Lewis, a pianist who could not read but played with A.J. Piron, encouraged Zutty. Zutty names the good musicians in Piron's band, including Pete Bocage.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yes, yes. Well when you went to New Orleans, now who had really taught you drums by the time you get your first professional job?
Oh well, I'll have to say Steve Lewis.
Yes, Steve Lewis. He encouraged me a lot. We played the drums, because we used to play little house parties and things like that.
'Purple Rose of Cairo.' And old Steve couldn't read, boy, and he played with all those good musicians.
He'd got a good ear then.
Yes, he must have had an ear.
Naturally Piron (Roth?) had the violin and give him those little (parts?) and things like that. Of course everybody in that band was a good musician. Like Pete Bocage (Roche?).
